# `Q-22-11` — Limits Command Ignored

> `\limits` or `\nolimits` was applied to something other than a big operator or a function name, so it has no effect.

## What this means

`\limits` and `\nolimits` choose whether the scripts of an operator such as `\sum` or `\lim` sit above and below it or beside it. Applied to an ordinary symbol they do nothing; quarto-math drops the command and reports it.

## Why this happens

Common causes: `x\limits_1` where `x` is a plain variable, or the command placed before the operator instead of after it.

## How to fix it

Place `\limits` right after the operator it modifies: `\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}`.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
